properties.Description: Shoma Group plans a 16-story building in Coral Gables, the first known Live Local Act project in the city where manicured lawns and Mediterranean Revival architecture are the norm. –– Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 8395 Northwest 27th Avenue in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
properties.Description: In West Little River, developer Pablo Castro –– who is little known in South Florida but has a long history in real estate in Spain –– and his local partner Laura Tauber plan South Florida's biggest approved Live Local Act project. Spanning over 4,000 apartments in seven towers, The HueHub will have amenities for families such as a center helping children with homework and a library. Under an agreement with Miami-Dade County unions, the majority of apartments will be for county employees, police officers, firefighters, hospitality workers, educators and health care workers. –– Lidia Dinkova

Tulip Developments Group –– a partnership among Amit Kort, Ofir Gabriel, Karl-Ulrich Ansorg of Berlin-based Ansorg Development and Yakov Elbaz of Royal Tulip Group –– scored approval for a 499-unit Live Local Act project on this Edgewater site, increasing the property's value. Tulip Developments has the site on the market, first listing it for $32 million in February and then increasing the asking price to $34 million this summer. Although many investors are obtaining Live Local Act project approval to bost sites' values, Tulip Developments "isn't opposed to" bringing its Edgewater project to fruition, according to the broker marketing the site. –– Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 6007, 6013 and 6015 Northwest Seventh Avenue, and 6056 Northwest Sixth Court
properties.Description: Integral Group, based in Atlanta, is seizing on two government initiatives for its planned South Florida affordable and workforce rental housing projects: Florida's Live Local Act and Miami-Dade County's Rental Assistance Demonstration program. The Live Local Act awards developers with property tax breaks and the right to build bigger projects, and the Rental Assistance Demoonstration program allows the county to partner with private firms to modernize aging, cash-strapped public housing complexes. In Miami's Liberty City, Integral plans a 170-unit project under the Live Local Act and in Homestead, it plans a 160-unit complex under the ental Assistance Demonstration program. — Lidia Dinkova
In Delray Beach, Kolter Group plans a 386-unit Live Local Act project. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 7501 and 7553 Northeast Second Avenue in Miami
properties.Description: Under the Live Local Act, developers can build up to 1,000-unit projects. Yet, Alejandro Velez's Midtown Capital Partners plans a smaller project with 348 units in the Little River neighborhood. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 2110, 2118 and 2134 North Miami Avenue, as well as 2101, 2129 and 2135 Northwest Miami Court
properties.Description: In Wynwood — a Miami neighborhood where property owners, planners and other stakeholders went to great lengths to craft development regulations that preserve its character, including limiting heights to 12 floors — Bazbaz Development wants to build a 48-story Live Local Act tower. It's one of two Live Local projects Sonny Bazbaz's firm plans in Wynwood. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: Southwest 214th Street and U.S. 1/South Dixie Highway
properties.Description: Pablo Buttice, son of the famous late Argentine soccer goalkeeper Carlos “Batman” Buttice, and Martin Racca, president of Argentine firm RCC Emprendimientos, want to build the first tower in Goulds under the Live Local Act. The plan is for a 25-story, 300-unit building in the south Miami-Dade neighborhood primarily home to low-rise apartment buildings, houses and shopping plazas. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 1515 and 1525 Northeast Miami Place, 75 Northeast 15th Street, and 1502, 1512 and 1516 Northeast First Avenue in Miami
properties.Description: Attorneys David Cohen and Liam Krahe, through the SF QOZ Fund I they lead as co-managing principals, and their partners want to build a Live Local Act project with luxury and workforce apartments on an Opportunity Zone site in Miami they purchased from Genting Americas. Genting, a Malaysian conglomerate, originally had planned a casino in the Omni district in Miami but never received the necessary approvals. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 2400, 2412 and 2418 North Miami Avenue, 29 Northwest 24th Street and 48 Northwest 25th Street
properties.Description: A major provision of the Live Local Act allows developers to building bigger projects with administrative approvals, bypassing public hearings, if they include affordable and workforce apartments. In Wynwood, a Miami neighborhood where heights traditionally were limited to 12 stories, this has opened the door for several planned massive projects with towers. On this site, LivWrk proposes a three-tower, 45-story project with over 1,000 units. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 23815 South Dixie Highway in unincorporated Miami-Dade
properties.Description: Since the Live Local Act was approved in 2023, many developers filed plans for projects and few have actually started construction. Exceptions include Beacon Hill Property Group, which this year started building a 112-unit Live Local Act project with two three-story buildings in Princeton. — Lidia Dinkova

"You had fun designing it": A Miami projects review board had good things to say about this Anillo. Toledo. Lopez-designed Live Local Act project in Edgewater. Developer Gonzalo Espinosa wants to build the 328-unit tower without maximizing the height the Live Local Act allows him. Under the state law he can build an 80-story building, but he opted for a 36-story project. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 10710, 10750 and 10800 Southwest 211th Street in Cutler Bay,
properties.Description: After signing a 99-year lease with Miami-Dade County for a portion of South Dade Government Center, David Martin's Terra increased the size of its project to a total of 724 units, using the Live Local Act, from its previous plan for 674 units. Terra had submitted an unsolicited proposal to Miami-Dade Commissioner Danielle Cohen Higgins to develop the site in 2023. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 190 Northwest 79th Avenue in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
properties.Description: In May, Miami-based Keystone Holdings Group — led by Miguel Mouriz, Reinaldo Mouriz and Enrique Puig — filed a pre-application for an 18-story, 477-unit Live Local Act project in the Fontainebleau neighborhood neighborhood of unincorporated Miami-Dade County. — Lidia Dinkova

Related Urban, the affordable housing arm of the Pérez family's Related Group, wants to extend its existing lease for a public housing site near West Little River to 99 years in order to redevelop the existing public housing buildings with a 316-unit Live Local Act project.  — Lidia Dinkova

Develop or sell? Retail investor and Miami Heat minority owner Raanan Katz supersized the development potential of his Sears site in Miami to over 1,000 units, and then quickly listed the property on the for-sale market, asking more than $100 million. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 2600 and 2630 Northeast 203rd Street in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
properties.Description: Boca Raton-based Group P6 is part of a crop of developers who seized on the Live Local Act to boost the size of their past project proposals. In Ojus, Group P6 plans a 21-story, 362-unit building, larger than its previous plan for an 18-story, 210-unit apartment building. — Lidia Dinkova

Miami's Health District already has been experiencing robust development. In one of the larger recently proposed projects, the Pérez family’s Related Group wants to develop an 842-unit Live Local Act project with a 27-story tower and a 31-story tower. The Miami-Dade County Public Health Trust, which owns the site, already approved Related as the winning bidder, awarding it a 99-year lease for the property. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 521 and 531 Southwest Seventh Street, Little Havana
properties.Description: Khashayar Khazai and Shane Shapiro of Sunny Isles Beach are betting in Miami's Little Havana, propising a 23-story, 166-unit Live Local Act tower in the neighborhood. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 2186 Northwest 13th Avenue and 1330-1342 Northwest 22nd Street in Miami
properties.Description: The Live Local Act has been so popular in the real estate community that now brokers are getting in on the development game, too. Commercial real estate brokers Lyle Stern and Kerry Newman, of Miami Beach-based Vertical Real Estate, propose a 24-story, 400-unit project in Miami’s Allapattah. — Lidia Dinkova

Athletes have long turned to real estate to invest and grow their wealth. Former Los Angeles Dodgers player Alex Guerrero wants to develop a 234-unit Live Local Act tower with a conspicuous colorful façade in Miami's Wynwood Norte area. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Developers: Related Group, BH Group, Pebb Enterprises
properties.Description: The  Pérez family's Related Group, the Toledano family's BH Group and Pebb Enterprise — a trio of development firms that's partnered on a few South Florida projects — plans the 33-story, 521-unit The Quay tower with a six-yacht marina on Fort Lauderdale's waterfront. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 6250 N Andrews Ave, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309
properties.Description: Pinnacle Housing Group is expected to start construction next year of a 196-unit Live Local Act complex with separate buildings for seniors and workforce tenants in Fort Lauderdale's Cypress Creek area. The development firm also received a $640,000 loan commitment from the city of Fort Lauderdale, contingent on Pinnacle qualifying for a 9 percent Low-Income Housing Tax Credits allocation from the state. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 791 Park of Commerce Blvd, Boca Raton, FL 33487
properties.Description: Oak Lane, led by Bhavin Shah, plans a Live Local Act project next to its headquarters in Boca Raton with 226 apartments and 17 townhouses. — Lidia Dinkova

properties.Address: 838 Northwest 79th Street in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
800 Northwest 13th Avenue, 780 Northwest 13th Court and 1389 Northwest Seventh Street in Miami
1200 Northwest 57th Avenue in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
Southwest 117th Avenue and the busway that runs along West Dixie Highway in Goulds
Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino in Hollywood
Northwest 27th Avenue and Northwest 54th Street in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
southeast corner of Northwest Sixth Avenue and Northwest 26th Street

properties.Developers: Alberto Fernandez Falcon, Rene Sanchez and Sam Jazayri
properties.Address: Northwest 27th Avenue and Northwest 46th Street in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
Northwest 27th Avenue and Northwest 123rd Street in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
3180 Biscayne Boulevard, 3195 Northeast Second Avenue and 220-250 Northeast 32nd Street in Miami
properties.Description: Crescent Heights, led by Sonny Kahn, Russell Galbut and Bruce Menin, plans Nema, a two-tower, 1,030-unit Live Local Act project in Edgewater, with 412 units in a separate workforce tower. An earlier version called for 1,300 units.

Crescent Heights revised its Live Local Act plan for 824 Alton Road in Miami Beach to a 39-story tower with 149 units, 72 of them workforce rentals, up from 31 stories and 120 units. Russell Galbut withdrew three other Miami Beach Live Local projects on Oct. 13, 2026; this one was not among them.

Allied Partners plans a 38-story tower with a hotel, 90 condos and 60 workforce rentals on the site of the 1937 Savoy Hotel in South of Fifth, using the Live Local Act and the state's Resilience and Safe Structures Act.

DFRE, led by Daniel Dias and Laura Weinstein-Berman, is building The Triangle, an eight-story, 112-studio Live Local Act project in the Miami Health District with every unit for households earning up to 120 percent of the area median income. Completion is expected in early 2028.

Rybak Development plans a 25-story, 262-unit Live Local Act rental tower in downtown West Palm Beach, with 40 percent of units affordable and most units micro-apartments, on the site of an assisted living facility.
An unidentified developer filed a pre-application for a 25-story Live Local Act tower near North Flagler Drive with 36 workforce rentals and 41 condos, including an 8,500-square-foot penthouse.
A three-tower, 765-unit Live Local Act project, Terrasse, is proposed to replace a former Winn-Dixie in Fort Lauderdale, with 306 workforce units.

Affiliated Development started construction on The Cove, an eight-story, 376-unit Live Local Act project in Fort Lauderdale, after landing a $74 million loan from Pacific Life. Fifty-five percent of units are workforce housing; completion is slated for 2028.

properties.Address: 209 North Sapodilla Avenue, West Palm Beach
properties.Description: Steve Ross' Related Ross plans its first Live Local Act project, an eight-story, 191-unit building near downtown West Palm Beach with nine affordable for-sale townhomes, restricted to households earning 30 to 80 percent of the area median income.

properties.Address: 3150 and 3160 Mundy Street and 3181 Douglas Road, Coconut Grove
properties.Description: Related Urban wants to replace most of an aging public housing complex in Coconut Grove with two towers, Magnus Grove and Stirrup Plaza, totaling 750 apartments under the Live Local Act, which requires at least 40 percent below-market units.

Hollywood approved Related Group's beachfront Portofino Hollywood under the Live Local Act, with market-rate condos and 84 workforce rentals on a city-owned site Related leases. Residents sued in June 2026 to block it.

properties.Address: 2627 and 2691 Northeast 203rd Street in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
properties.Description: The Faith Group filed a pre-application to replace its Aventura Offices and Medical Center building with a 14-story, 376-unit Live Local Act project in unincorporated Miami-Dade.

McDowell Housing Partners plans Ekos Melrose Manor, a 110-unit Live Local Act apartment complex for households earning up to 80 percent of the area median income, on a brownfield site in Fort Lauderdale.

Russell Galbut and partners plan to redevelop Fort Lauderdale's Galleria Mall into a nine-tower mixed-use district with more than 3,000 apartments under the Live Local Act, drawing resident opposition.

properties.Address: 120 South Dixie Highway and 321-333 Datura Street, West Palm Beach
properties.Description: Billionaire Jeff Greene's first Live Local Act project is a 25-story, 366-unit mass-timber apartment tower in downtown West Palm Beach that keeps two historic facades of a former fire station.

An entity tied to Russell Galbut and Lefferts' Mendy Chudaitov plans a 15-story, 29-unit Live Local Act building on a narrow South Beach lot; the Miami Beach Planning Board approved its mechanical car elevator.
Ascentris and Zom broke ground on Hazel Doral, a seven-story, 380-unit Live Local Act project replacing a Doral office building, backed by a $92.3 million construction loan.
Florida Value Partners' FVP Forum Owner LLC is in pre-application for two eight-story buildings with 302 units in Kendall, at least 40 percent workforce housing under the Live Local Act.

properties.Address: 9001 Northwest Seventh Avenue and 663 Northwest 90th Street in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
properties.Description: Barbara and Sebastian Cobas plan NoMi 7|90, a 19-story, 480-unit project near El Portal combining the Live Local Act with Miami-Dade's workforce housing program; 192 units are for households earning up to 120 percent of the area median income.

properties.Developers: Pebb Capital, Maxwelle Real Estate Group and Russell Galbut
properties.Description: Pebb Capital's joint venture is suing Miami Beach, alleging the city is blocking its plan to turn the vacant Bancroft Hotel into a Live Local Act project with 249 apartments and 38 hotel rooms.
Surfside's first Live Local Act proposal is an 11-story building with 22 residences and 11 hotel rooms on a post office site in an area capped at four floors.

properties.Address: 2607 and 2617 South Federal Highway, Boynton Beach
properties.Description: Affiliated Development started construction of The Dune, a 336-unit Live Local Act project in Boynton Beach with 198 workforce units, after a $73 million loan from Pacific Life.
Coral Rock scored a $54 million Citibank construction loan for Dulce Vida, an eight-story, 227-unit Live Local Act building in Allapattah where every unit is at affordable or workforce rents.
Miami's Urban Development Review Board approved Namdar Group's 42-story, 1,011-unit Live Local Act tower in Brickell, with 405 workforce apartments and 599 micro-units.

properties.Address: 3311 and 3327 Northwest Second Avenue, 169 Northwest 33rd Street and 182 Northwest 34th Street, Miami
properties.Description: ABH Developer Group, led by Alexis Bogomolni, won design approval for Wyn Park, a 36-story, 293-unit Live Local Act tower in Wynwood Norte.

properties.Address: 1210 Northwest Second Avenue and 211 and 223 Northwest 12th Street, Miami
properties.Description: An entity tied to KYU restaurant co-founder Alan Omsky won design approval for a 55-story, 498-unit Live Local Act tower in Overtown with 200 below-market apartments.
Plantation approved Midtown Capital's site plan for a six-story, 300-unit apartment project with 60 affordable units on an office park parking lot, under the Live Local Act.
The Caltagirone brothers' Calta Group won approval for Anatomia, a 30-story Live Local Act tower in Allapattah with 289 condos and 210 below-market apartments.
